h1: The 6 Best Mattress Vacuums Under $100 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Mattress Vacuum Under $100: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six mattress vacuums under $100, compared on suction in kPa, UV-C light, heat and weight to clean beds and sofas.
summary: The uwant 18Kpa is our best overall mattress vacuum under $100, with the strongest listed suction. The heated purple model with a dust sensor is the best feature pick, the cordless HEPA model is the most portable, and the 1.2kg 13Kpa unit is the lightest.
intro: The number on the box that sells most mattress vacuums is suction, and it is also the number buyers misread. A kPa rating tells you how hard the motor pulls, not how well the UV light kills anything, and a lamp that touches the fabric for a second does not do the job its marketing implies.

We reviewed eight handheld bed vacuums, all under $100, and ranked six on the spec sheet: suction, motor speed, UV-C wavelength, heat, filtration, weight and whether the unit is corded. We kept claims to what the listings state and treated UV as a bonus.

products.name: uwant 18Kpa Mattress Vacuum Cleaner 60000RPM Tap Bed Vacuum Set of 1
products.verdict: The highest listed suction here at 18 kPa, plus a 60,000 RPM motor.
products.description:
The uwant mattress vacuum lists 18 kPa of suction, the highest in this group, and a 60,000 RPM motor. For a tool whose job is pulling dust out of dense fabric, pull is the first thing to look at.

It ranks above the 16 kPa models because the extra suction is the most concrete performance edge on paper. The cost is that the listing leans on motor speed rather than extras like heat or a dust sensor, which the purple model offers.

Buy it if raw suction matters most for a thick mattress. The caveat is that kPa figures are manufacturer claims, so treat them as a ranking tool rather than a promise.
products.skipIf: You want heat or a dust sensor.

products.name: Mattress Vacuum Cleaner with 275nm UV-C Light & 149℉ Heat, 16Kpa Powerful Suction Bed Vacuum for Pet Hair & Dander, Smart Dust Sensor, Anion & Aromatherapy, Corded for Bed, Sofa, Couch, Purple
products.verdict: Heat, a dust sensor and UV-C at the $25 to $50 tier.
products.description:
This purple mattress vacuum pairs 16 kPa suction with 275nm UV-C light, 149 degree Fahrenheit heat and a smart dust sensor, plus anion and aromatherapy functions. It is corded and aimed at pet hair and dander.

It ranks second because the uwant has stronger suction, but this model adds more features in a cheaper tier. You get the sensor and heat; you give up cordless freedom.

Pick it for a pet household. The caveat is that the unbranded listing makes support harder to judge.
products.idealFor: Pet owners who want extra features cheaply.

products.name: FEPPO Mattress Vacuum Cleaner PRO, 4-in-1 16Kpa Bed Vacuum with UV-C Light
products.verdict: A 4-in-1 design with 16 kPa suction and UV-C light.
products.description:
The FEPPO Mattress Vacuum Cleaner PRO is a 4-in-1 design with 16 kPa suction and UV-C light, in the $50 to $100 tier.

It ranks third because suction matches the cheaper models while the price is higher, so the 4-in-1 versatility is the selling point. Compared with the standard FEPPO below, it adds more functions.

Choose it if you want one tool for several surfaces. The caveat is that the listing is short on detail about what the four modes are.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting one tool for beds and sofas.

products.verdict: Cordless with HEPA filtering, UV-C and ultrasonic function.
products.description:
This cordless handheld lists 16 kPa suction, 253.7nm UV-C light, a HEPA filter and ultrasonic function, in the $25 to $50 tier. It cleans beds, sofas and cribs without a cord.

It ranks fourth because cordless runtime is not listed, while corded rivals run indefinitely. You trade guaranteed power for freedom to move.

Pick it for quick cleans in several rooms. The caveat is battery life, which the listing does not detail.
products.idealFor: People cleaning sofas, cribs and beds.

The Teant MV-Blue mattress vacuum lists 16 kPa suction and 253.7nm UV-C light in the $50 to $100 tier.

This handheld lists 13 kPa suction, UV-C light, LED headlights, high heating tech and a 1.2kg weight, in the $25 to $50 tier.

It ranks last because 13 kPa is the lowest suction here. The upside is weight and headlights that show where dust hides.

Pick it for spot cleaning and lighter hands. The caveat is the weaker pull on thick mattresses.

whatMatters.detail: Kilopascals measure how hard the motor pulls, and higher numbers lift more dust from fabric. Ratings run from 13 to 18 kPa in this group. Compare the figure in the title, and remember it is a maker claim.

UV-C bulbs are marketed for sanitizing, but effect depends on exposure time and distance. Treat the light as a bonus rather than the reason to buy. Check the wavelength, such as 253.7nm, in the listing.
Some models heat to about 149 degrees F to help with dust mites. It is a helpful extra but not a substitute for washing bedding. Look for a stated temperature.
Corded units run as long as you need, while cordless ones depend on the battery. For a whole bed, a cord reaches most places. Check the listing for runtime if you pick cordless.
A lighter tool tires your hand less, and a HEPA filter traps fine dust instead of blowing it back. Check the weight in kg and look for the word HEPA.

faq.q: Does a mattress vacuum replace washing sheets?
faq.a: No. It removes surface dust and debris. Keep washing bedding on your usual schedule.

faq.q: What is the biggest buying mistake?
faq.a: Choosing on UV claims. Check suction and filter first.

faq.q: Is the uwant worth it over a 16 kPa model?
faq.a: If your mattress is thick, yes. For standard beds the cheaper options do fine.

faq.q: How often should I use one?
faq.a: A pass every few weeks is a reasonable routine, more often with pets.
Empty the dust bin and rinse or replace the filter as the maker directs.

faq.q: Can I use it on sofas?
faq.a: Most listings cover beds, sofas and couches. Check the title.

finalTake: The uwant 18Kpa is the mattress vacuum most buyers under $100 should choose because suction is the part that matters. Pick the heated purple model for pets, the cordless HEPA unit for portability, and the 1.2kg model for easy handling. Treat UV as a bonus.
